chunks.title: Verbal Reasoning practice
chunks.text:
Book is to reading as fork is to _____.
A book is used for reading. A fork is used for eating.
chunks.source: Havan authored demonstration practice — not an official UAT paper

chunks.title: Verbal Reasoning practice
chunks.text:
All engineers in a group study mathematics. Hana is an engineer in that group. What must follow?
The rule applies to every engineer in the specified group. Hana belongs to that group, so Hana studies mathematics.
chunks.source: Havan authored demonstration practice — not an official UAT paper

chunks.title: Grammar practice
chunks.text:
Choose the correct sentence.
The present perfect uses has with a singular third-person subject and the past participle finished.
chunks.source: Havan authored demonstration practice — not an official UAT paper

chunks.title: Grammar practice
chunks.text:
Choose the correct completion: Neither the lecturer nor the students ___ absent.
With neither ... nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject. Students is plural, so are is correct.
chunks.source: Havan authored demonstration practice — not an official UAT paper

chunks.title: Vocabulary practice
chunks.text:
Which word is closest in meaning to meticulous?
Meticulous means showing great care and attention to detail. Thorough is the closest choice.
chunks.source: Havan authored demonstration practice — not an official UAT paper

chunks.title: Vocabulary practice
chunks.text:
Choose the antonym of abundant.
Abundant means present in large quantities. Scarce means insufficient or difficult to find.
chunks.source: Havan authored demonstration practice — not an official UAT paper

chunks.title: Reading Comprehension practice
chunks.text:
Passage: The library extended its opening hours during examination week. Attendance increased, but borrowing remained unchanged. Which statement is directly supported?
The passage explicitly says attendance increased. It does not say borrowing increased.
chunks.source: Havan authored demonstration practice — not an official UAT paper

chunks.title: Reading Comprehension practice
chunks.text:
Passage: Although solar panels cost money initially, they can reduce electricity expenses over time. What is the main idea?
The contrast between initial expense and later reduced electricity costs supports the possibility of savings over time, not guaranteed savings for every household.
chunks.source: Havan authored demonstration practice — not an official UAT paper

chunks.title: Quantitative Problem Solving practice
chunks.text:
A price rises from 200 birr to 250 birr. What is the percentage increase?
Increase = 250 - 200 = 50 birr. Percentage increase = (50 / 200) × 100 = 25%.
chunks.source: Havan authored demonstration practice — not an official UAT paper

chunks.title: Quantitative Problem Solving practice
chunks.text:
Solve $3x + 7 = 22$.
Subtract 7 from both sides: 3x = 15. Divide by 3: x = 5. Substitution gives 3(5) + 7 = 22.
chunks.source: Havan authored demonstration practice — not an official UAT paper

chunks.title: Analytical Reasoning practice
chunks.text:
What comes next in the sequence 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ...?
The differences are 4, 6, 8, 10. Continuing this pattern gives a difference of 12, so the next term is 30 + 12 = 42.
chunks.source: Havan authored demonstration practice — not an official UAT paper

chunks.title: Analytical Reasoning practice
chunks.text:
Three students A, B, C stand in a line. A is before B, and B is before C. Which order is possible?
Combining A before B and B before C gives the unique ordering A, B, C.
chunks.source: Havan authored demonstration practice — not an official UAT paper

chunks.title: Equivalent open propositions
chunks.text: Open propositions P(x) and Q(x) are equivalent over a universe U when P(a) and Q(a) have the same truth value for every a in U. Equivalence depends on the chosen universe. For U = {-1, 1}, x² = 1 and |x| = 1 are both true for every member.
chunks.source: Havan authored demonstration note — not an official module
